assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern
assertions.evidence: Four @TableTest methods: splitsShipmentsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress, splitsShipmentsByStockAvailability, choosesWarehouseCombinationMinimizingShipmentCount, keepsCompanionProductsTogetherWhenPossible.

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: Expectation cells like '["camera,lens"]', '["IMMEDIATE:[camera,lens]"]', '["W1:[camera,lens]", "W3:[battery,mic]"]' vary per row and are not verbatim copies of input cells nor constant across rows.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: @Description for availability states 'BACKORDERED and PRE_ORDERED both ship WHEN_AVAILABLE' and for warehouse/companion tables explains 'fewest-shipments combination' and 'tie for fewest shipments', all outside the method body.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules.
assertions.evidence: Fulfillment/address table has 6 rows including two interaction rows ('Items sharing an address group together, others split' and 'Delivery split by address, plus a separate pickup item') though only one optional interaction row is warranted; availability table repeats the 'not held' obligation separately for backordered and pre-ordered ('In-stock item not held for a backordered item' and 'In-stock item not held for a pre-ordered item'), exceeding the minimal 4 rows.

assertions.text: Fulfillment method splitting is represented in a @TableTest
assertions.evidence: Row 'Delivery and pickup items always split | ["camera:DELIVERY:Addr-A", "mug:PICKUP:"] | [camera, mug]'

assertions.text: Delivery address splitting is represented in a @TableTest
assertions.evidence: Row 'Same type, different delivery addresses | ["camera:DELIVERY:Addr-A", "watch:DELIVERY:Addr-B"] | [camera, watch]'

assertions.text: Availability splitting is represented as its own @TableTest
assertions.evidence: void splitsShipmentsByStockAvailability(...) table with rows for IN_STOCK, BACKORDERED, PRE_ORDERED items.

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation is represented as its own @TableTest
assertions.evidence: void choosesWarehouseCombinationMinimizingShipmentCount(...) table with W1/W2/W3 stock columns and Shipments? output.

assertions.text: Companion product grouping is represented as its own @TableTest
assertions.evidence: void keepsCompanionProductsTogetherWhenPossible(...) table with Companions column and tie-breaking rows.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method includes all output columns for its concern in the same table.
assertions.evidence: Warehouse table's Shipments? column e.g. '["W1:[camera,lens]", "W2:[mic]"]' encodes both warehouse assignment and shipment count together.

assertions.text: A compound output is expressed as a native TableTest list/map/set, not a hand-rolled string encoded with brackets/colons and assembled/parsed by a helper.
assertions.evidence: Shipments? cells like ["IMMEDIATE:[camera,lens]"] and ["W1:[camera,lens,mic]"] built via describeByAvailability/describeByWarehouse string-concatenation helpers.

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario"

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Shipments?', 'Groups?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Shipments?, Shipments?, Shipments?, Shipments?

assertions.text: Scenario names describe the business situation, not 'Test case 2'.
assertions.evidence: "Companions win a tie between equally minimal warehouses", "No single warehouse covers everything, split is forced"

assertions.text: Column names use business/domain language.
assertions.evidence: Columns: 'Scenario | Items | W1 Stock | W2 Stock | W3 Stock | Companions | Shipments?'

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 4 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 4 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the outcome depends on and held constant every row must be visible as a column or named in @DisplayName/@Description.
assertions.evidence: splitsShipmentsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress has no @Description and fixes all items to IN_STOCK/W1 via 'inventory.addStock("W1", item.getProductId(), StockStatus.IN_STOCK)' with no mention of this held fact.

assertions.text: A comparison criterion (ordering, tolerance, subset matching, normalisation) applied by the assertion must be stated on the published surface.
assertions.evidence: describeByItems/describeByAvailability/describeByWarehouse all call '.sorted()' before assertEquals, but no description or column states shipments are compared without regard to order.
